svg.title: Multi-factor authentication, and three ways attackers go after it
svg.desc: Top: MFA combines something you know (a password), something you have (a phone or token), and something you are (a fingerprint). Bottom: an attacker who phished the password bombards the victim with push prompts until one is approved (MFA fatigue), relays one-time codes through a fake login page in real time, or talks the help desk into resetting the victim's MFA. A FIDO2 security key, bound to the real site, defeats phishing and relay.
svg.text: Multi-factor authentication, and three ways attackers go after it

g.text: a tired victim finally taps Approve
Fix: number matching, alert on bursts
password and code typed into the fake
page are replayed to the real site
Fix: callback and strong caller checks
Phishing-resistant MFA: a FIDO2 key signs only for the real site, so fake pages and relays get nothing.
